text: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month of the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt. He said:
"Take a census of the whole community of Israel, clan by clan and family by family, listing every male by name, one by one—

versions.text: "Take a census of the whole community of Israel, clan by clan and family by family, listing by name every male,
versions.explanation: The phrase לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָם ("head by head, one by one") belongs at the end of verse 2, but the translation has moved it to the beginning of verse 3. For oral reading verse by verse this displaces content across the verse boundary; better to keep it where the Hebrew places it.

text: twenty years old and upward—everyone in Israel fit for military service. You and Aaron are to register them by their divisions.

versions.text: one by one, twenty years old and upward—everyone in Israel fit for military service. You and Aaron are to register them by their divisions.
versions.explanation: "One by one" renders לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָם, which stands at the close of verse 2; removing it here avoids duplication once verse 2 is corrected, and the verse then begins cleanly with the age requirement.

text: One man from each tribe shall assist you, each the head of his family.
These are the names of the men who will stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;
from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan."
These were the men appointed from the community, the leaders of their ancestral tribes, the heads of the clans of Israel.
So Moses and Aaron took these men who had been designated by name,

and on the first day of the second month they assembled the whole community. The people registered their ancestry by clan and family, and all the men twenty years old and upward were listed by name, one by one,
just as the LORD had commanded Moses. And so he counted them in the wilderness of Sinai.

The descendants of Reuben, Israel's firstborn: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, one by one, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Reuben was 46,500.
The descendants of Simeon: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were counted and listed by name, one by one, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Simeon was 59,300.
The descendants of Gad: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Gad was 45,650.
The descendants of Judah: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Judah was 74,600.
The descendants of Issachar: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Issachar was 54,400.
The descendants of Zebulun: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Zebulun was 57,400.
From the sons of Joseph—the descendants of Ephraim: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Ephraim was 40,500.
The descendants of Manasseh: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Manasseh was 32,200.
The descendants of Benjamin: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Benjamin was 35,400.
The descendants of Dan: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Dan was 62,700.
The descendants of Asher: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Asher was 41,500.
The descendants of Naphtali: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
The number from the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.
These were the men counted by Moses and Aaron and the twelve leaders of Israel, each one representing his family.
So all the Israelites twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were counted by their families.
The total came to 603,550.
The Levites, however, were not counted among them by their ancestral tribe.
Then the LORD said to Moses:

versions.text: The LORD had said to Moses:
versions.explanation: The Hebrew wayyiqtol וַיְדַבֵּר introduces a new divine speech in sequence, not a pluperfect flashback. "Had said" wrongly suggests the instruction preceded the census; "Then the LORD said" is accurate and reads naturally aloud.

text: "The tribe of Levi, however, you are not to count; do not include them in the census of the Israelites.

versions.text: "You are not to count the tribe of Levi or include them in the census of the Israelites.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew opens with the strong restrictive particle אַךְ ("only, however"), which marks Levi as an exception to the census just completed. The current rendering drops this contrastive force entirely, and the single long clause with "or" reads flatly aloud. Restoring the contrast also improves the oral rhythm by breaking the sentence into two beats.

text: Instead, put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle of the covenant law, with all its furnishings and everything that belongs to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings; they are to care for it and camp around it.
Whenever the tabernacle is to move, the Levites shall take it down, and whenever it is to be set up, the Levites shall raise it. Anyone else who comes near it must be put to death.
The Israelites are to camp by divisions, each in his own camp under his own banner.
But the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the covenant law, so that no wrath may fall on the community of Israel. The Levites are to keep watch over the tabernacle of the covenant law."
The Israelites did just as the LORD had commanded Moses; everything he commanded, so they did.

versions.text: The Israelites did everything the LORD commanded Moses; so they did.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has an emphatic double construction ("according to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so they did"), but "did everything ... ; so they did" reads as a stumbling repetition when spoken. Reordering keeps the intended emphasis while giving a clean cadence for oral reading.
